Name: Shannon Bicksler
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I definitely want to start using sentence stems. I think it might have helped to put these on the board even though I also had the slideshow up there. I think also that I should've done more discussion after each part. Getting students to engage in discussion has always been difficult for me. Just to see what the students got out of each article. I think overall it taught me to slow down and break things apart.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
I think the part that feels the most meaningful was when they were drawing the pictures. Just seeing them struggle but eventually get it and do well was nice. They were also excited about their pictures and explaining their reasons behind their drawings. I think it helped to build their confidence a bit which is something I'm always trying to do.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I notice some students who did not explain their reasoning but rather just stated information from the text that supported if they liked daylight savings time or not. In my mind an argument includes the reasoning on why it matters to me. So far the majority of students have used terms like "text 2 states" or "Fall back states". Some students definitely put more effort into this then others. I'm just interested to see what we will specifically be looking at and breaking down looking at these drafts.
